headlines.title: Firefighters battle Dutch Flat Fire in the Vallejo area
headlines.description: Firefighters were battling a vegetation fire near the border of Solano County and Napa County Saturday afternoon. The Dutch Flat Fire was burning around 5 acres in the wetlands near Kimberly Drive and Meadow Bay Drive, according to authorities. Evacuation orders were issued, per the American Canyon Police Department, but they were later lifted. Officials added the fire has a moderate rate of spread and structures are threatened at the head of it. They later said the forward progress was stopped with the assistance of Cal Fire helicopter water drops, but the incident remains active.

headlines.title: Firefighters battle vegetation fire in Fremont
headlines.description: Firefighters were battling a vegetation fire in Fremont Saturday afternoon, according to authorities. Authorities said the fire was initially burning approximately 2 acres in the 41400 block of Vargas Road in Fremont, but the fire later grew to reach 20 acres. Officials said the fire was burning in light flashy fuels at moderate rate of spread with no structures threatened. Shortly after, authorities said the forward progress of the fire was stopped.

headlines.title: National Weather Service issues beach hazard statement for Bay Area beaches
headlines.description: The National Weather Service issued a beach hazard statement for beaches across the San Francisco Bay Area and Central Coast from Saturday through Wednesday afternoon. The NSW says cyclones in the Eastern Pacific are pushing a long-period southerly swell toward the Pacific coastline. For that reason, they warned there will be an increased risk of sneaker waves and strong rip currents, with breaking waves of up to 10 feet at Bay Area beaches and the Central Coast from Saturday through Wednesday afternoon. The NWS warned people to stay off of jetties, piers, rocks and other waterside infrastructure, remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf and never turn their backs to the ocean. headlines.title: Four people shot after trying to intervene in argument in San Francisco
headlines.description: Four people were shot in San Francisco after trying to intervene in an argument between a man and a woman early Saturday morning, the police department said. San Francisco police said officers responded to the 900 block of Market Street regarding a shooting at approximately 12:51 a.m. Authorities said officers arrived on scene to find four men with apparent gunshot wounds. Paramedics transported victims to a local hospital for non-life threatening injuries, according to police. The police department reports a preliminary investigation determined that the victims attempted to intervene a verbal altercation between a man and a woman. The man then pulled out a firearm, shot the four victims and ran away, police said. The police department said no arrests have been made at this time. They encourage anyone with information is asked to contact the SFPD at 415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 and begin the message with SFPD.

headlines.title: Environmental Protection Agency gives update on Moss Landing fire cleanup
headlines.description: Thousands of batteries are still inside the Moss Landing Battery Plant after its fire in January 2025, according to the Environmental Protection Agency. The fire was ignited by an equipment faliure, but crew members have been working on safely removing the batteries for demolition. Officials said most of the batteries have now been removed, but about 5,000 are still in parts of the building that are too dangerous or difficult to reach. The agency says the demolition of the damaged building can begin once all of the batteries have been removed. headlines.title: Man dies after police shooting in Fremont
headlines.description: A man holding an apparent firearm at an assisted living facility died following a police shooting in Fremont Friday, the police department said. Police said dispatch received multiple calls at around 3:38 p.m. reporting a man with a gun at an assisted living facility on Walnut Avenue. Authorities said the man was reported to be holding a firearm and carrying a duffel bag. They added he was last seen in a meeting room reportedly holding two people hostage. Multiple police officers responded and found the suspect holding an apparent firearm, according to the police department. Authorities said an officer-involved shooting occurred, and the suspect had to be taken to the hospital where he was pronounced deceased. The facility says the man arrived after a family dispute, though police say they are not yet able to confirm that. Police said investigators contacted the California Department of Justice’s Police Shooting Investigation Team to take over the investigation upon examining the suspect’s weapon. Authorities added the investigation is ongoing, and no suspects are believed to be outstanding. They added they do not believe there is a threat to the public safety at this time.

headlines.title: Small fire sparks near Pleasanton as containment grows on nearby Little Fire
headlines.description: Friday afternoon, a car fire appeared to spread to a nearby hillside between Sunol and Pleasanton. Drivers going northbound on 680 approaching Happy Valley Road saw the flames and scorched hillside. While this brush fire only got up to 5 acres and was quickly contained, it sparked familiar fears for neighbors who recently were on alert for the Little Fire, which happened only a few miles away. The Little Fire, which started earlier this week and spread to a little more than 1,000 acres in the Pleasanton hills, is 90% contained as of Friday evening, Cal Fire said. Assistant Chief Steven Blythe with Cal Fire Santa Clara Unit said that the call came out about Friday’s fire at 3:19 p.m. He said that initial reports indicate the fire began underneath a car that was on 680, then spread to the grass on the surrounding hillside. Blythe said this fire is under investigation. The Koopmann family, who have a ranch just off of 680, confirmed that the fire did reach their property. However, the Koopmanns said that Cal Fire responded quickly and that together they were able to get the blaze contained without anyone getting hurt. While the firefight and the subsequent cleanup were going on, fire trucks blocked off several lanes of 680 northbound, and evening traffic was backed up for hours. In the Happy Valley neighborhood nearby, charred grass is visible on the eastern hills where the Little Fire extended earlier in the week. Residents in Happy Valley were not among those ordered to evacuate during the Little Fire, but many were prepared to and felt anxious seeing the large plumes of smoke not too far away. “I drove home and realized the smoke was basically coming from the hillside behind our neighborhood,” recalled neighbor Kristina Johnson. She said that other fires have started in the area as well, related to incidents on the freeway. Many neighbors are feeling especially on alert after the Little Fire and were nervous to see smoke or receive alerts Friday. “When I got the Watch Duty alert [Friday], I was hoping it was somewhere far away,” said neighbor Dominic Gaiero. “Then, I saw it was right here, just down the street, and I got really concerned,” he continued. As for the Little Fire, Cal Fire crews will continue working on it overnight Friday night into Saturday morning, hopeful they will reach 100% containment this weekend.

headlines.title: ‘I love my community': Oakland rapper Mistah F.A.B. speaks out after arrest
headlines.description: Oakland rapper Mistah F.A.B says he has no regrets after police arrested him on illegal fireworks charges on Wednesday. “This is the sacrifice you make when you stand up for the community,” he said. The high-profile artist and community activist, whose real name is Stanley Cox, posted a video on the Fourth of July that prompted police to search his house and businesses. According to court documents, police found a stolen gun at Mistah F.A.B’s home and multiple boxes of fireworks at his downtown Oakland business Dezi’s Lounge. “I love my community. As I say if I’m guilty of anything it’s organizing and galvanizing and bringing a safe space for community members from all walks of life to enjoy a good old Fourth of July firework show,” he said. Mistah F.A.B says setting off fireworks is a neighborhood tradition in Oakland. He insists the event was safe. “I’m guilty of organizing an event bringing a community together in a village, a kumbaya. So we can have a fireworks show in our neighborhood, where kids can feel safe. I’m guilty of that?” he said. “That’s not a way to bring joy. It’s about public safety. I grew up here when it comes to fireworks were out of control,” City Councilmember Noel Gallo said. Gallo says he’s surprised and disappointed. Especially because he says Oakland has worked so hard to send a clear message that fireworks are dangerous and illegal in the city. In fact, fireworks sparked multiple fires in the city over the Fourth of July and left the streets a complete mess. Gallo helped clean up much of the aftermath. “I think definitely he needs to apologize to the community, the community that we represent that we’re here to serve that has supported us in the past and there needs to be certainly an apology to the neighborhood,” Gallo said. Mistah F.A.B says he’s staying positive and urges the community to do the same. He says he’s focusing on his next community project: a school supply giveaway next month. “Showing up for the community and this is what happens. I wanna let the community know I’m not gonna stop showing up for y’all. I’m gonna continue to keep putting on for these kids. Just so these kids can see a positive light in their community,” Mistah F.A.B said. The artist pleaded not guilty in court Friday morning to two misdemeanor charges of possession of dangerous fireworks and one misdemeanor charge of receiving stolen property.

headlines.title: Antioch house fire leaves 2 people hurt
headlines.description: Two people were hurt following a house fire in Antioch on Friday, according to Contra Costa Fire. The fire broke out at a home on Putnam Street, not far from Park Middle School. Two people were taken to the hospital, one of them by air ambulance, according to authorities. Putnam Street remains closed and people are being asked to avoid the area while firefighters make sure the fire is completely out.

headlines.title: San Quentin inmate featured in SFMOMA art exhibition
headlines.description: When the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA) celebrates this weekend’s opening of a new exhibition by an up-and-coming artist, the guests at the shindig won’t include the artist himself. That’s because artist Orlando Smith will be 16 miles away, locked in San Quentin Rehabilitation Center. Smith, who also goes by the name O. Smith, is the first incarcerated artist to hold a solo exhibition in the modern art museum, which opened in 1935. Smith has made a name for himself outside prison walls with his graphic art drawings, which tell poignant stories about life within the prison system as well as national and international politics. “So far I’ve done about 50-something graphic novels,” Smith said by phone from the prison. The gallery show features drawings and posters by Smith, done in his comic book style. “I was in sixth grade the first time I saw the original King Kong versus Godzilla,” Smith said. “And I wanted to draw that King Kong.” Artist Orlando Smith has spent the last 30 years in prison. An exhibition of his graphic arts drawings opens this weekend in SFMOMA. Smith began drawing in the sixth grade growing up in South Central Los Angeles, inspired by Marvel Comics and Batman movies. He drew all the time, even entering a few art contests. As a young adult, he was pinstriping cars when his clients began to pay him in drugs. He began using and selling crack cocaine, which became a gateway into burglaries. In and out of prison, he eventually earned eight life sentences through California’s Three Strikes Law. “From there I went into criminality and it landed me here,” Smith said. Behind prison walls, art became his escape. His illustrations documented life in prison, the plight of older prisoners, as well as what he called “protest posters,” which touched on societal issues in and out of prison. When the pandemic hit San Quentin, forcing more than two years of lockdown, Smith turned to his pens to tell the stories. Every day alarms went off, cries of “man down” as COVID ravaged the prison. His art veered into the realm of illustrative journalism. “I just started documenting my daily actives, what I seen, how unprepared the entire world was for the pandemic,” Smith said. Smith’s images, which he’d mail to friends, began to appear in art shows around the Bay Area, aided by Empowerment Avenue, a group that uses art, journalism and film to create opportunities for people in prison. Smith’s art grabbed the attention of SFMOMA curator Nancy Lim, who arranged for his solo show in the museum. A self-portrait in prison is part of Orlando Smith’s art exhibition opening this weekend in SFMOMA. “Orlando’s work has been on view around the country and the Bay Area for a number of years now,” said Lim, who first saw Smith’s art in 2021. “I realized how extraordinary it would be to be able to see his works in concentration.” The exhibit features some 50 of Smith’s works, touching on themes of racial inequality, civil rights abuses and what he sees as failures of the prison system. Smith recently had his sentence readjusted and now has the potential for parole. He said in recent years he came to grips with his own childhood trauma and the regret for his victims. Now, his steps toward rehabilitation will also include an exhibition in a major art gallery. “It’s an opportunity, that’s a blessing,” Smith said. “I’m just grateful.” The exhibit opens Friday and runs through June 27, 2027.

headlines.title: Bay Area gas prices are on the rise
headlines.description: Gas prices in the Bay Area, along with the rest of California and the nation, keep climbing, according to a weekly fuel report from AAA’s regional office in Walnut Creek. Average fuel prices around the Bay Area include $5.76 in San Francisco, $5.58 in Oakland, and $5.57 in San Jose, according to the statement. At $5.57 per gallon, a 17-cent increase from last week, California had the highest average gas price in the nation, according to the report. “Rising crude oil prices are behind the spike at the pump,” said AAA Mountain West Group spokesperson Aldo Vazquez in a statement. “Volatility along the Strait of Hormuz and instability in the region have pushed oil prices into the $90 per barrel range and could continue driving up costs during the second half of the summer.” The largest component of gas prices at the pump is the cost of crude oil, and the second largest share of retail gas prices is refining costs, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration in the Department of Energy. The price of crude oil on the global market is constantly changing in response to supply, demand, geopolitics and other factors, according to EIA. National gasoline production increased last week, averaging 9.7 million barrels per day, according to EIA. Gasoline demand also increased last week from 8.84 million to 8.94 million barrels per day, which is about 376 million gallons per day. Daily updates of gasoline prices in California, including major metropolitan areas, are available at gasprices.aaa.com.

headlines.title: Young Black innovators in Oakland learn to build AI tools to help the community
headlines.description: Young Black innovators in Oakland are putting artificial intelligence to work for their community. Kids as young as 11 spent the summer learning to build AI-powered apps designed to solve real neighborhood problems that were important to them. For six weeks, 26 young Black men from 11 to 25 in Kingmakers of Oakland learned coding, prompt engineering, and software development while building live AI-powered apps focused on issues affecting their communities. A first for the program. “For our Kings to move from just passively receiving all that’s on their phone and all the programs have to offer them to thinking critically what they are doing with it, how they can create something different and how it’s impacting us as a community,” Kingmakers of Oakland Program Director Kahlil Chatmon. Working in small teams called Tribes, each group focused on a different community issue—from youth substance abuse and education to resources for foster youth transitioning into adulthood. They also visited Google’s San Francisco campus for a deeper look at AI. “For our Kings, it’s about building something that can better impact our experience and also create and produce that our people can use that are for us, by us,” Chatmon said. For Tribe leader Willie Rodgers, a former Kingmakers student now attending Morehouse College, his team’s project focused on closing the resource gap between Oakland’s public and private schools by creating a petition to push for change. “We are all from Oakland, but we all have different backgrounds, so the fact that we came together to create something that can truly create a change,” he said. Another Tribe focused on creating a tool for immigrants to report ICE activity. Their app provides a private community watch map and connects users with immigration resources while prioritizing privacy. “Once we figured out the end goal, using a user’s location for only 30 seconds and once they make a report that data gets wiped off, and stuff like that, they felt relief and pretty proud that they were able to build this app,” Tribe Chief Sanusi Signateh said. Friday, the young innovators will showcase and pitch their apps to technology leaders, with plans to continue developing their ideas throughout the year. Organizers say the goal is to give them the tools to become leaders in tech and beyond to drive change.
